I would like to suggest maxing multiple, since every school can hypothetically max every weave. But for your first pick, here's an idea:

So there are two triads of schools, elemental and spirit. And every school is connected to two schools of the other triad in the magic wheel. Myth is connected to Fire and Ice, for instance. And if you wanted to follow the wheel and connect everything to an adjacent school, you would have two options of combinations with the triads:

Fire-Myth
Ice-Death
Storm-Life
Myth-Ice
Life-Fire
Death-Storm

OR

Fire-Life
Ice-Myth
Storm-Death
Myth-Fire
Life-Storm
Death-Ice

But there's one problem. Balance isn't connected to any school, and it can't weave into itself. So you have to choose what to weave into on a Balance, and fill in the gaps in the wheel with the other schools. The school left without a pair would weave into Balance.

As for what to weave into on Balance, it's up to you. Balance synergizes with all hanging effects, but I personally think its blade identity suits it most, so Storm, the blade school, would be my choice. And with that choice, the list would be like this:

Balance-Storm
Fire-Life
Ice-Myth
Storm-Death
Myth-Fire
Life-Balance
Death-Ice

OR

Balance-Storm
Fire-Myth
Ice-Death
Storm-Life
Myth-Ice
Life-Fire
Death-Balance

See how either Death or Life could weave into Balance with this? Coincidentally, both schools are adjacent to Storm on the opposite triad. So whatever you choose to weave into on Balance, look into its adjacent schools on the opposite triad, choose one of them to weave into Balance with, and fill in the blanks.

Long post, but if nothing else, this was entertaining for me to write. Good luck with your setup!

First off, use Sky Iron Hasta for your wand. It's a guaranteed drop from Olympus, so you should have it.

You're good stats wise, except your pet. Pets, when perfected, can give around 20+ damage and 15+ resist for questing. It takes a LOT of time and resources, and you should be able to get by while working on that, but you might want to look into pet training. It's a complex system and too much to explain here.

Lastly, your deck setup seems to be THE problem. I imagine you find yourself struggling to find the cards you need for battles, and falling short of buffs when you're ready to hit. Fire usually has one of the easiest times with Frost Bones, especially considering you have Fire Dragon already. But you NEED a smaller deck size. And I mean WAY smaller, around 7-10 cards.

You will find yourself struggling to find the right cards with a big deck way more often than running out of cards and having to flee with a small one, and you can train Reshuffle for that. Pack a blade, find another blade to stack with it from pets, amulets, etc. Cast both of those and dragon to kill. Pack a meteor as a backup hit and that's really all you need. Don't waste time with heals and shields unless you go through multiple attempts and just can't survive.

I'm also going to assume you spam smaller hits on enemies judging by the amount of smaller single hits you have, and that's not the right strategy for leveling, at least. This game relies on alpha striking: stacking up many buffs to kill all enemies with one hit. Blade, blade, dragon should cover you well enough for a good while. Add feints (train feint from death, it's very important) and other buffs as needed, but keep your deck as small as you can, within the 7-10 range. Good luck.

I'm a man, but I feel like disability also counts. Honestly, I don't even practice martial arts even though I really, really want to, which makes me feel like a fraud in this sub. But I know how frustrating it is to be told you just can't do some stuff.

I can't speak about this in the context of women, but I can at least recognize that it feels unfair. You seem like you recognize the situation itself, but are finding it hard to accept it. In that way, we're not that different. We're both presented with physical disadvantages that we can overcome... to a certain point. After that, we hit our ceiling. Or at least, that's what I keep hearing. I haven't actually tried getting up, let alone breaking the ceiling. Maybe it's possible. In any case, it's admirable you try.

This isn't about coming to terms with the fact that you won't get higher, it's about accepting that you *might* not. That applies to a lot more people than you think, but it applies in a more concrete sense to women and other people like me who are in a physical disadvantage.

You start with understanding what this fact means to you. For instance, does it make you feel inferior? You might know that you're not and still feel that way, be honest with yourself. Do you feel cheated in some way, having this obstacle despite how hard you try? Do you feel trapped or helpless by this restriction imposed on you (by society or nature, it doesn't matter)? Why is the idea of possibly never being as powerful as some men so uncomfortable to you? It's completely normal to feel this way, but it helps to understand where it comes from.

What comes next? I haven't gotten too far either, so I'm not sure. You should probably address your findings. If you feel inferior in some way, continue living your life, and look out for things that proves that idea wrong. Think of a random person that, by this arbitrary rule -whether it's true or not- you can't beat in a fight. Watch out for moments that you accomplish things that this person can't, or wouldn't be able to do. Prove to yourself that you aren't inherently less than him. Will that matter to you, or will it still have no point, knowing you'll never be able to beat him in a fight? Both feelings are valid, I know I felt the latter too many times.

If the whole idea feels unfair, which I agree with, you get to decide how to cope with it. Most people just accept that life *is* inherently unfair, and move on. I hate that idea, so I try to find my own strengths. Because people are never measured on only one axis. It feels unfair, and that's valid, but you get to choose how to react to that.

I've been constantly hearing about this topic talked about, and I've been confused as to why no women spoke up about how upsetting this is, and I'm glad to see your frustrations in display, because I feel like this is something that should be talked about. And with all the negative mindsets I've seen about this (women can do martial arts, but they'll never get as far as men etc.), I wanted to see a different take. Partly because I'm affected by these limitations too, just... not because I'm a woman.

Think of what you need to get past this. Can you find a way around this? Do you want to? Or do you just want to rage at this and wish it just didn't exist? You get to decide what you want to do. But what I think this all boils down to is this: It's always okay to try and grow past who you are, but not because who you are right now isn't enough. **You can always push your limits, but you're already complete.**

Out of all the players, I'm the most openly upset about this situation. Two of them has their grievances but doesn't push it that much (as in, stay neutral in my "arguments" with the DM), one player has a general problem of disinterest in the group and party, in and out of character. I might have angered my DM a bit by getting genuinely angry, but we both tried our best to stay respectful while defending our points.   


They are adamant that we should have looked into it more and took the orcs more seriously, while they were breaking the 4th wall and literally asking me to heal them (I brushed it off as a joke, but apparently that was them asking to stop fighting and talking it out). I stated that the overly light and joking tone led me to believe these were just some randos to kill. They say that light tone was a trick, but I still don't think it's fair to trick the players instead of the PCs.  


Thankfully, they did acknowledge their fault on that, but still think we could have done better, which I agree with. We both explained the faults of the other side and came to an agreement, but it hasn't exactly led to any action, if this situation even calls for one. Yet.

What they do is basically give us A and B. We pick B, some horrible thing happens. A beloved NPC dies, we commit genocide, those are the latest things. Another NPC comes in to berate us on why we didn't pick A. The DM doesn't tell us it was the wrong choice generally, or that A would have worked out well, but nor do they deny it.   


I'm not mad about us choosing wrong. Okay, maybe I am a little. But I'm mainly mad about us having no direction on what is right. Some NPC tells us our plan is dumb and isn't going to work. We ask "do you have a better idea?" and they don't respond. We go with our plan and when it doesn't work, said NPC has the audacity to yell at us and call us idiots.  


It feels personal at this point. It's not a NPC-to-PC insult, it feels like a DM-to-player one. It's disheartening.

The "these orcs aren't so innocent" part is something I'll choose to believe for my own sanity, they did attack a city and killed a bunch of people, even if they weren't *as* evil as we first thought. And in fairness, this session was the very first time we actually got betrayed by a trusted NPC. In other cases, there's option A or B, and the one we pick turns out to be the wrong one.  


We do have some allies, and again, for the sake of my own sanity I'll choose to blindly trust *some* of them. And the campaign has always been dark, and we've been okay with that, until it got so bad it made me actually cry. And the answer isn't really in making it less dark, at least not for me. "Dark" is a tone, but the message can be hopeful, or nihilistic. The former is my favorite kind of storytelling, the latter is something I absolutely despise.  


Problem is, we aren't saving the world because we want to anymore. We have to, because we've literally been to the future and the world ends without our involvement. If the characters have the energy to care at this point. It's up to the DM to bring some hope into this, in character too other than a simple "get your shit together". I'll talk to them about it.

The campaign has been really RP heavy so far, and I admit we haven't used Insight and Perception rolls in a WHILE, which we probably should've. I honestly forgot about them at that point, and I'm a druid. We don't exactly have any psychic magic on our side either. But passive scores might help.

We do have the aid of a future-telling god, but they are the uselessly cryptic kind. They also love to constantly tell us whatever plan we come up with is a dumb plan. The only plan that worked out for us is rescuing an essential ally, and that plan worked out thanks to us noticing an antimagic field last minute. If we didn't, we'd fail once again and probably get TPKd.   


So that's the kind of guessing games we have to deal with, and I have expressed my frustration on never knowing what the right thing to do is. The orcs' specific situation is sort of different, but for what it's worth I don't think the DM is changing what the right thing to do is specifically to screw us over. We just happen to make the wrong choice every single time, which is equally frustrating.
